newsitem.title: JAPAN: More Japan local govts halt deals with DKB--paper.
newsitem.headline: More Japan local govts halt deals with DKB--paper.

text.p: An increasing number of Japan's local governments are supending business with Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) due to its suspected illegal dealings with racketeers, a Japanese business daily said on Friday.
It added that some customers in overseas markets may also suspend business with the bank.
Japanese telecoms giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) had also decided to suspend part of its business with the bank, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
Prosecutors on Thursday arrested four DKB officials on suspicion of illegal loans of 11.78 billion yen to racketeer.

Nihon Keizai said that, in a widening move among local governments to penalise DKB, the Hokkaido prefectural government and the city of Sapporo had decided not to include DKB in syndication groups for their bonds.
Sapporo has also transferred 100 million yen in deposits from DKB to another financial institution, the paper said.
Nihon Keizai said DKB's deposits as of the end of May may have fallen by tens of billions of yen from the end of March, mainly due to withdrawals by local governments.
The paper said more local governments were expected to suspend business with the bank.
Officials from the local governments and NTT were not immediately available for comment on the report.
